- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), often peaking 1–2 days too early.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model fails to recognize when prices are drifting toward historical averages.
- Tends to ignore downward momentum in the 3rd–5th day of the forecast, especially after a spike.
- Overconfident in short-term volatility — forecasts show higher variance than actual, particularly in the last 5–7 days.
- Often misjudges the “tail” of the forecast — last 3–5 days are frequently too low, especially if the prior 10 days were high.
- Sensitive to recent high prices — model reacts too aggressively to recent peaks, leading to overcorrection or overshoot.
- Lags in recognizing downward trends — model delays turning negative or low forecasts until 3–5 days after the trend starts.
- Underestimates the impact of policy or market events — model doesn’t adjust for sudden regulatory or supply shocks unless they’re recent.
